description: Roadmap for the card authorization and double-entry ledger project, sequencing the three-week build against the implementation plan, known gaps, and ADRs in docs/design-doc.md.
note: docs/design-doc.md is the source of truth. Where this roadmap and the design doc disagree, the design doc wins; task detail below follows it.

status_legend.in_progress: Started; specific remainder recorded in the task's `remaining` field.
status_legend.backlog: Optional stretch; only if the core is solid.

invariants.I1: For every transaction, the sum of all ledger entries equals zero.
invariants.I2: available_balance = current_balance - sum(active_holds), at all times.
invariants.I3: An authorization can be captured at most once, for exactly its authorized amount.
invariants.I4: Replaying a request with the same idempotency key returns the original response, never a second effect.
invariants.I5: Expired holds (default 7 days) release automatically, without manual intervention.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.goal: Prove the path API Gateway -> shared layer -> boto3 -> DynamoDB -> response, with CI/CD and IaC in place before any domain code is written.
phases.exit_criteria: A trivial service deploys itself on merge to main, with lint, format, and tests gating the PR.

tasks.title: Python project skeleton
tasks.detail: uv-managed project pinned to Python 3.13 (matching the Lambda runtime), ruff for lint and format, pytest with unit/integration/e2e split and markers, Makefile targets.

tasks.title: Shared Lambda layer
tasks.detail: utils (API Gateway payload 2.0 helpers, Decimal-safe JSON encoding), errors (ApiError hierarchy mapped to status codes), dynamo (cached boto3 resource, endpoint override for tests, required_env).

tasks.title: Toy items service
tasks.detail: POST /items and GET /items/{item_id} over a one-key placeholder table. Deliberately shaped nothing like the real single-table design so it can be deleted rather than migrated.
tasks.notes: Delete once the authorization service replaces it (see p1-16).

tasks.title: Terraform stack
tasks.detail: HTTP API (payload format 2.0) with access logging and throttling, Lambda on arm64/python3.13, shared layer packaged inside `plan` via archive_file source blocks, DynamoDB toy table, per-function IAM role with ARN-scoped inline policy, explicitly created log groups with retention.

tasks.title: Remote state and OIDC deploy roles
tasks.detail: Bootstrap root (local state, applied by hand) creating the versioned, encrypted S3 state bucket with native lockfile locking, plus gha-payledger-plan and gha-payledger-apply roles whose trust policies split read-only from write on the OIDC `sub` claim.

tasks.title: CI pipeline
tasks.detail: ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest -m 'not e2e' with junit upload; terraform fmt/validate with -backend=false so no credentials are needed. DynamoDB Local image pre-pulled so testcontainers' start timeout is not spent on the pull.
tasks.notes: Target was CI on day 2, not day 10. Met.

tasks.title: CD pipeline
tasks.detail: terraform plan on PR under the read-only role with the plan posted as a PR comment; terraform apply on push to main under the write role. Privilege split enforced by STS trust policy, not by workflow conditions.

tasks.title: Integration test harness
tasks.detail: Session-scoped DynamoDB Local container via testcontainers, readiness polled against the DynamoDB API itself, fake AWS credentials injected session-wide so boto3 cannot reach a real account, per-test table create/drop.

tasks.title: HTTP client smoke suite
tasks.detail: Requests against the deployed API with assertions, including the check that an unrouted method is rejected by API Gateway before Lambda is invoked. `make http-env` writes the live URL into a gitignored env file.

tasks.title: Repository documentation
tasks.detail: README with architecture diagrams and deploy instructions, CLAUDE.md for agent context.

phases.name: Week 1 - Core correctness
phases.goal: authorize / capture / void working end to end, idempotently, on the real single-table design.
phases.exit_criteria: The three write operations work end to end and idempotently, with the balance invariant verified under randomized input.

tasks.title: Domain model with Pydantic
tasks.detail: Account, Merchant, Authorization, LedgerEntry, Idempotency record. Amounts are integer minor units; Decimal only at the presentation boundary; no floats anywhere.

tasks.title: Ledger DynamoDB table in Terraform
tasks.detail: Single table with PK/SK per the design doc's key schema, GSI1 for lookup-by-id, sparse expiry GSI keyed on expires_at for holds only, TTL attribute on idempotency records, PITR enabled, stream enabled (NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES) ready for week 2.

tasks.title: Customer-managed KMS key for the table
tasks.detail: CMK with rotation; every role touching the table also gets kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey conditioned on kms:ViaService for DynamoDB.
tasks.notes: Also a missing line item in the cost model (see p4-03).

tasks.title: Validate the single-table design against the access-pattern list
tasks.detail: Walk all eight access patterns against the key schema before writing data-access code: get account, get merchant, get authorization, list authorizations by account newest-first, list ledger entries for a party by date range, get every entry of one transaction, look up idempotency by key, find expired holds.

tasks.title: Data-access layer
tasks.detail: Key encoding (ACCT#/MERCHANT#/AUTH#/TXN#/IDEM# prefixes stay internal and are never exposed to or accepted from clients), item serialization, query helpers.

tasks.title: Idempotency layer
tasks.detail: Start with the Powertools decorator, then read its source to understand the conditional-write mechanics. Must cover: request_hash mismatch on a reused key returns 422 rather than replaying, IN_PROGRESS vs COMPLETED so a crash-after-write-before-response is recoverable, response snapshot returned verbatim, TTL of 24-48h.

tasks.title: POST /authorizations
tasks.detail: TransactWriteItems: conditional decrement of available_balance (this ConditionExpression IS the overdraft protection), Put of the hold with an absolute expires_at resolved from expires_in_days, Put of the idempotency record.

tasks.title: Positional CancellationReasons handling
tasks.detail: Read TransactionCanceledException's CancellationReasons by index to tell insufficient funds from a replayed idempotency key. Conflating them is the easy bug and they are different HTTP responses.

tasks.title: POST /authorizations/{id}/capture
tasks.detail: Six-item TransactWriteItems: debit account current_balance, credit merchant payable_balance, two ledger entries, status PENDING->CAPTURED guarded by ConditionExpression, idempotency record. Capture is all-or-nothing for the full authorized amount and deliberately does not re-check sufficient funds.

tasks.title: POST /authorizations/{id}/void
tasks.detail: Release the hold: restore available_balance, move status to VOIDED under a PENDING guard, write the idempotency record.

tasks.title: GET /accounts/me/balance
tasks.detail: Strongly consistent GetItem returning both current and available balance. Its IAM role gets GetItem only - no Query, no index.

tasks.title: Expired-hold sweeper
tasks.detail: Scheduled Lambda querying the sparse expiry GSI and releasing due holds. Chosen over TTL-driven stream events because TTL deletion timing can lag by hours.
tasks.notes: Flagged in the design doc's known gaps: success criterion 5 currently has no mechanism behind it, and no component appears in the diagram.

tasks.title: Cognito user pool and JWT authorizer
tasks.detail: Strict password policy (12+ chars, upper/lower/number/special) and MFA. sub maps directly to account_id. Until this lands the API is public, which is why the URL is kept out of git.

tasks.title: Ownership rules on authorization-scoped routes
tasks.detail: account_id derived from the validated sub, never from body or path. capture/void load the authorization and reject a mismatch with 404, not 403 - a 403 confirms the id exists and turns the endpoint into an enumeration oracle. A request body carrying account_id is rejected with 400 rather than ignored.

tasks.title: Error-response contract
tasks.detail: Status codes and error bodies for insufficient funds, already-captured, expired hold, idempotency-key conflict, and payload mismatch on a reused key.
tasks.notes: Listed in the design doc's known gaps.

tasks.title: Per-function IAM roles for the new services
tasks.detail: One role per function, ARN-scoped, GSI ARNs named separately from the table ARN. Explicit Deny on dynamodb:DeleteItem everywhere except CompensateLedger, whose delete is scoped by LeadingKeys to IDEM#*. Retire the toy service, its table, and its role.

tasks.title: Property-based test: the ledger always balances
tasks.detail: Hypothesis test asserting, after any random sequence of valid operations, that every transaction's entries sum to zero and that available_balance recomputed from the holds matches the materialized value.
tasks.notes: This single test is worth more than fifty unit tests: it exercises I1 and I2 under randomized operation sequences.

tasks.title: Integration tests for the write path
tasks.detail: Against DynamoDB Local: idempotent replay, concurrent authorize racing the available-balance guard, double capture rejected, void after capture rejected.

phases.name: Week 2 - Distributed systems
phases.goal: The async path: streams to EventBridge, the capture saga with real compensation, and the Aurora read model.
phases.exit_criteria: A capture flows through the saga, lands in Aurora, and one request can be traced end to end in X-Ray across async boundaries.

tasks.title: Versioned event schema
tasks.detail: Pydantic models doubling as the schema definition for everything published to the bus.

tasks.title: DynamoDB Streams to EventBridge
tasks.detail: Stream forwarder Lambda publishing to the bus, with the stream ARN and bus ARN scoped in its role.

tasks.title: SQS queues and DLQs per consumer
tasks.detail: SQS between EventBridge and each consumer for buffering and retry, DLQ on every consumer, ReportBatchItemFailures so one poison message does not re-drive nine healthy ones.

tasks.title: Capture saga state machine
tasks.detail: Step Functions Express: FraudScreen -> SubmitSettlement -> NotifyCustomer, with CompensateLedger reachable from the first two failing. A failed notification never reverses a real payment. Retry policy on SubmitSettlement must fit inside the 5-minute Express ceiling, or the workflow times out before reaching compensation.

tasks.title: Express execution logging
tasks.detail: Log level ALL including execution data, to CloudWatch Logs. Non-negotiable: Express retains no queryable execution history otherwise, and the runbook depends on answering 'which state did this authId fail in?'. Keep the saga payload minimal (ids and a decision) because it lands in logs by design.

tasks.title: Simulated FraudScreen and SubmitSettlement
tasks.detail: Deterministic fraud rules plus a random-injection knob to force the FLAGGED path; settlement misbehaving on command via SETTLEMENT_TEST_MODE (always_fail, flaky, always_reject) so compensation can be triggered deliberately rather than waited for.

tasks.title: CompensateLedger
tasks.detail: One TransactWriteItems: restore both balances, two new opposite-sign entries under a new txnId (originals never touched), CAPTURED->REVERSED guarded so a duplicate compensation is a no-op, and delete the capture's idempotency record so a replay re-executes and fails the PENDING guard instead of returning a stale success.

tasks.title: VPC and network boundary
tasks.detail: Private subnets for anything reaching Aurora, gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB, no NAT Gateway on any route.
tasks.notes: Missing from the design doc's diagram; also a cost guardrail.

tasks.title: Aurora Serverless v2 and RDS Proxy
tasks.detail: Postgres cluster with min capacity 0 ACU, CMK encryption set at cluster creation, no public accessibility, reached only through RDS Proxy with TLS enforced. Create in week 2, not week 1.

tasks.title: Aurora projector Lambda
tasks.detail: psycopg v3 through RDS Proxy, consuming from SQS. Streams are at-least-once, so the projector upserts on the record's monotonic sequence number to discard replays rather than double-apply. Parameterized statements only - inlined literals would put customer data on the Performance Insights top-SQL screen.

tasks.title: Rebuild-from-scratch capability
tasks.detail: Replay the table from a DynamoDB export to rebuild the projection when projector logic changes or the read model needs repair. The runbook's projection-lag procedure depends on this existing.

tasks.title: GET /accounts/me/transactions
tasks.detail: Cursor-based paginated history served from Aurora, eventually consistent. Its role gets rds-db:connect as a read-only user and nothing else.

tasks.title: Observability
tasks.detail: Powertools structured logging (explicit fields only, never the raw event or response), X-Ray tracing with no identifiers in annotations, EMF metrics, correlation ID generated at the edge and propagated through every hop including async.

tasks.title: Dashboard and alarms
tasks.detail: CloudWatch dashboard; alarms on DLQ depth, p99 latency, projection lag, and Aurora ACU utilization - the four the runbook is written against.

tasks.title: Secrets Manager with rotation
tasks.detail: The acquirer secret SubmitSettlement reads. Its role gets secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on that ARN and no DynamoDB access at all.
tasks.notes: Listed as a missing design-doc subsection.

tasks.title: CloudWatch Logs data protection policy
tasks.detail: Managed data identifiers masking email and phone if one ever reaches a log group. A backstop for a mistake, not a primary control.

phases.name: Week 3 - Break it on purpose
phases.goal: Induce the failures the runbook describes, build the tools to recover from them, and measure the cost/latency assumptions the ADRs assert.
phases.exit_criteria: Three failure modes can be described: what was induced, what the system did, and what changed as a result.

tasks.title: Chaos: kill a Lambda mid-saga
tasks.detail: Confirm the saga's at-least-once semantics hold and that a second run of compensation is a no-op rather than a double reversal.

tasks.title: Chaos: throttle DynamoDB
tasks.detail: Verify the standard retry mode absorbs it and that what surfaces to the caller is a sane error, not a stack trace.

tasks.title: Chaos: poison the queue
tasks.detail: Confirm ReportBatchItemFailures isolates the poison message from healthy ones. If it does not, that is the bug the runbook says to fix.

tasks.title: Chaos: force a TransactionCanceledException
tasks.detail: Exercise every cancellation reason position and confirm each maps to the right HTTP response.

tasks.title: DLQ replay CLI
tasks.detail: Python + boto3 tool to inspect messages without removing them, edit, discard, and re-drive. The runbook's DLQ procedure assumes it exists.

tasks.title: k6 load test
tasks.detail: Cold starts, throttling behavior, and projection lag under sustained write pressure.

tasks.title: Measure provisioned concurrency vs SnapStart vs cold starts
tasks.detail: ADR-3 asserts a choice against an unstated target. Measure both options under load rather than assuming, and note that provisioned concurrency bills per hour regardless of traffic - a cost floor, not a variable cost.

tasks.title: Generate real IAM policies from CloudTrail
tasks.detail: IAM Access Analyzer policy generation, run after chaos testing has exercised the rarely-taken paths (compensation, DLQ redrive) - anything never invoked is absent from a generated policy.

tasks.title: Write up the induced failures
tasks.detail: Three failure modes, what the system did, what changed. Feed anything learned back into the runbook.

phases.name: Deliverables and documentation
phases.goal: The written artifacts that make this a lead-level project rather than a working service.
phases.exit_criteria: The design doc reads as a review-board document with no self-declared gaps left open.

tasks.title: Architecture Decision Records
tasks.detail: Six ADRs, each stating the decision, the alternative rejected, the reasoning, and the condition for revisiting: DynamoDB over Aurora, Step Functions over choreography (and Express over Standard), provisioned concurrency/SnapStart over cold starts, single-table over multi-table, reversal entries over mutation, EventBridge over direct SQS fan-out.

tasks.title: Runbook
tasks.detail: Ledger out of balance, DLQ filling, projection lag, Aurora at max ACU, RDS Proxy connection exhaustion - each with symptom, likely causes, diagnosis, mitigation, and follow-up.

tasks.title: Cost model
tasks.detail: 100 TPS sustained, where the cliff is, which line item dominates, what the lever is.
tasks.remaining: KMS is absent entirely and, with a CMK on DynamoDB at this request volume, may be large enough to reorder the table below Step Functions. Cognito has no line either.

tasks.title: Design doc as a review-board document
tasks.detail: Close the gaps the doc declares against itself.
tasks.remaining: SLOs (ADR-3 and the cost model both reason about p99 against an unstated target); data retention for ledger entries, Aurora rows, and log groups; regional failure behavior with RTO/RPO; encryption in transit as its own subsection; abuse controls (throttling, WAF); audit logging (CloudTrail); diagram omissions (Streams node, SQS/DLQs, notification target, VPC boundary, projector labelling).
tasks.notes: The error-response contract and the expired-hold sweeper are also on this list; they are tracked as p1-15 and p1-12 because they are code, not prose.

tasks.title: README with architecture diagram and one-command deploy
tasks.detail: What it is, current status, target vs actual architecture, getting started, deploy, API, invariants.

tasks.title: Answer the interview-grade questions cold
tasks.detail: How transact_write_items differs from a database transaction and where it falls short; idempotency record written but the Lambda died before responding; why reversal entries; how the projector stays correct under at-least-once delivery; provisioned concurrency vs SnapStart vs cold starts; diagnosing a wrong available balance in production; why not just Aurora; why RDS Proxy.

phases.name: Cost guardrails
phases.goal: Keep the three weeks inside a $10-30 total build budget.
phases.exit_criteria: No surprise line item on the monthly bill.

tasks.title: AWS Budget alarm at $20
tasks.detail: Day one, before writing any code. Not yet in Terraform.
tasks.notes: Overdue against its own schedule - the stack is already deployed.

tasks.title: No NAT Gateway
tasks.detail: ~$32/month plus data processing, and the most common way people get surprised. Gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB instead; interface endpoints cost ~$7/month each if one is genuinely needed.
tasks.notes: Nothing is in a VPC yet; holds by default. Becomes a live constraint at p2-08.

tasks.title: DynamoDB on-demand
tasks.detail: Never provisioned at this scale. On-demand is right for spiky low-volume dev usage; the cost model notes it stops being right at steady 100 TPS.

tasks.title: CloudWatch retention on every log group
tasks.detail: Set explicitly in Terraform. The default is never-expire and it accumulates silently.
tasks.notes: Currently 14 days (var.log_retention_days); the design doc's development-cost guardrail says 7. Decide which, and apply it to every group added from here.

tasks.title: Aurora min capacity 0 ACU, pause verified
tasks.detail: Scale-to-zero only works if nothing holds a connection open - a stray RDS Proxy connection or a forgotten debugging session keeps it warm and billing. Verify the pause actually happens rather than assuming it.

tasks.title: X-Ray sampling at 5-10%
tasks.detail: Once past initial debugging.

tasks.title: Daily terraform destroy in week 3
tasks.detail: At the end of each day when not actively testing. Table definitions and Lambda code are in git, so re-apply is a five-minute operation.

phases.name: Optional stretch
phases.goal: Only if the core is solid.

tasks.title: MSK Serverless replacing EventBridge for one flow
tasks.detail: Partitioning, ordering, and consumer-group semantics hands-on. Has a real hourly floor - do it in a tight, deliberate window.

tasks.title: A second consumer on the event stream
tasks.detail: Proves the schema actually supports fan-out rather than just claiming it does.

tasks.title: Schema registry with an explicit compatibility policy
Multi-region read replica design
tasks.detail: As a written design, not an implementation. The write-up is the valuable artifact.

tasks.title: Port the DLQ replay CLI to Go or Java
tasks.detail: Low-risk way to sample another ecosystem once the core is solid.
